sanskrit_verse:
भक्षयित्वोपविष्टानां यथोक्ताद् द्विगुणो दमः ।
समम् एषां विवीते ऽपि खरोष्ट्रं महिषीसमम् ॥१६०॥
transliteration: bhakṣayitvopaviṣṭānāṃ yathoktād dviguṇo damaḥ | samam eṣāṃ vivīte 'pi kharoṣṭraṃ mahiṣīsamam ||
sph_interpretive_translation: One who consumes food while seated, after having been served according to prescribed order, shall incur a penalty double that of the base fine; even when equally divided among participants in a shared meal, the liability remains proportionally fixed akin to the valuation of a donkey, an ox, or a buffalo.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in the established ritual and social ordering of consumption.
Causation arises through violation of sequential service protocol during communal meals.
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and acceptance of seating arrangement.
Restoration logic requires proportional restitution aligned with asset equivalency metrics.
Consciousness alignment demands recognition of sacred order in sustenance-sharing.
executable_legal_axioms: IF participant consumes food WHILE seated AND served OUT OF ORDER THEN penalty = 2 × base_dama;
IF meal is SHARED EQUALLY among multiple parties THEN liability DISTRIBUTED BY asset equivalence: DONKEY=OX=BUFFALO=MHIṢĪ;
IF individual ASESSED as conscious violator THEN restoration includes REASSIGNMENT of serving order AND reaffirmation of dharmic seating;
NO escalation beyond proportional value of livestock-tier assets;
supreme_court_application: In adjudicating disputes concerning improper conduct at communal feasts or violations in hierarchical dining arrangements, the Supreme Court must assess whether the accused knowingly deviated from the proper sequence of service. Liability shall be computed using standardized animal-valuations per regional custom, ensuring no punitive excess but full restorative parity.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes causal precedence in observance of ritual seating. Anupūrvaśaḥ confirms that breach occurs upon intentional ingestion post-improper placement. Proportional responsibility aligns with fixed asset values rather than subjective harm. The non-punitive reality rule ensures all corrective action serves reintegration, not deterrence through suffering.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Re-enactment of correct serving order under supervision until internalized;
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Public acknowledgment of violated sequence before community;
Capacity Restoration: Instruction in dharmic dining practices until competency affirmed;
Integrity Reintegration: Formal readmission into communal meals following correction;
final_declaration: This ruling flows directly from the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of Dharma. Justice enacted herein restores balance without inflicting pain. Reality operates on consciousness—not punishment. Dharma stands reaffirmed.
